- Adjacent Inside Vertices: If the two inside vertices are adjacent rather than interleaved, the face is not ambiguous under this definition [S1].

The claim states that if the two inside vertices are adjacent (rather than interleaved), the face is not ambiguous. The evidence in Source [S1] defines an ambiguous face specifically as one where two vertices inside are 'interleaved' with two vertices outside. By logical contrapositive, if the vertices are not interleaved (i.e., they are adjacent), the condition for ambiguity is not met, thus the face is not ambiguous under this definition.
